I'm not a huge expert with guns, I usually just buy what I like and keep it the way it is. I have an M&P9 2.0 compact that I want to upgrade but have questions for yell.

Should I consider changing the trigger?

Thanks in advance!

Sight color is a preference, red seems harder to pick up at night than green to me (come to think of it, I've never seen red night sights, but it wouldn't surprise me). Green is right in the center of the visible spectrum, making it easy to pick up.

Threaded barrels are of course available for any popular gun... But why? Are you buying a suppressor? You know that'll take months (maybe over a year) and cost more than the gun, right? (Barrel, suppressor, booster, and tax stamp)

If you can put up a 4 inch group at 10 yards and wonder how to get to the next level, you might consider the trigger. The factory trigger is decent should be fine unless you have a specific complaint.

He might be talking about fiber optic sights.

I have one on my G23 in yellow but I can swap it out for red/green/white as well.

Yes, sorry. Optic sights. Or glow/night sights. I had one on my Glock but that came with it.

I've considered a ghost ring sight but heard they need to be close to the eye to be practical.

Don't confuse fiber optic sights and electronic dot sights. Way different animal.

Otherwise your looking at tritium night sights, eg meprolight or Trijicon.

Fiber optic sights do not glow in complete darkness. They gather ambient light and "glow", the more light available the brighter they are, in theory.

Yeah, sight colour is mostly preference.

Threaded barrels are available but I would skip that for now.

If you really want to do the trigger Apex seemed to be the go to.

Honestly, if your newish to the game or just don't shoot much I would leave it alone.

The best upgrades you can start with is a REAL gunbelt, quality holster, a way to carry a spare mag, ammo & range time.

Maybe even consider taking a class.

Really get to know the gun before you start making all kinds of crazy upgrades. That shit won't make you any better, repetition and practice will.

OWB everyday stuff I like Galco and Bianchi.

I've also had good luck with randrholsters on eBay.

You can ccw with OWB, just get your shirts in the tall option or buy the next size up.
